# Projects {.page-title}

Most of this work comes back to one idea: a system is only as useful as its honesty about its own errors. It runs through document intelligence, interpretability, data engineering, distributed systems, behavioral machine learning, LLM agent design and simulation. Each project has a short case study. Most also have a technical report with the experiment history, the metrics and the steps to reproduce the results, including the results that did not go my way.

Content review: **6 November 2026**. Test totals and benchmarks belong to the snapshots named on each page; they are not live status counters. Some older reports retain historical results and are labeled where newer releases supersede them.

## Document intelligence {.group-title}

One question runs through five projects: how do you read and sort business documents accurately, at a cost you can defend? I followed it from raw public data to a deployable service, and each project answers one part of it.

- **The data.** [Mailroom-Corpus-EDA](mailroom-corpus-eda.qmd) builds the 3,302-document corpus the others share, with a record of where every label came from and labels kept out of the text a model reads.
- **The design.** [Digital-Mailroom](digital-mailroom.qmd), my capstone with American Family Insurance, sends each document to the cheapest step that can handle it and scores the routing by fixed rules.
- **The model.** [Mailroom-ML](mailroom-ml.qmd) trains a ModernBERT classifier whose calibrated confidence decides which documents can skip the LLM.
- **The service.** [Mailroom Reloaded](mailroom-reloaded.qmd) rebuilds the design so that code, not a model, owns the control flow. A clean document costs exactly two LLM calls.
- **The no-training baseline.** [RVL-CDIP-Classifier](rvl-cdip-classifier.qmd) asks how far a general vision LLM gets on the standard benchmark with only a prompt, and what each page costs.

{{< include ../partials/diagrams/_ecosystem.qmd >}}

::: {.cards .cards-wide}
::: {.card cover="digital-mailroom"}
### [Digital-Mailroom](digital-mailroom.qmd)
[Capstone · American Family Insurance]{.kicker}

The capstone design: five Python packages and one LangGraph pipeline for document routing, prompt experiments, deterministic scoring, and deployment, trained and tested on a dataset I assembled from public sources.

[LangGraph]{.tag} [Docker]{.tag} [Dataset design]{.tag}
:::

::: {.card cover="mailroom-ml"}
### [Mailroom-ML](mailroom-ml.qmd)
[Training, evaluation & calibration]{.kicker}

A ModernBERT classifier that handles the easy documents quickly. It calibrates its own confidence, so it knows when to pass a document to an LLM.

[PyTorch]{.tag} [Calibration]{.tag} [ONNX]{.tag} [Modal]{.tag}
:::

::: {.card cover="mailroom-reloaded"}
### [Mailroom Reloaded](mailroom-reloaded.qmd)
[Agentic pipeline · deployable rebuild]{.kicker}

The mailroom as one service you can deploy. A deterministic driver runs CrewAI agents in a fixed order, escalates hard cases by fixed rules, and records every decision in an audit log.

[CrewAI Flows]{.tag} [FastAPI]{.tag} [OpenTelemetry]{.tag}
:::

::: {.card cover="rvl-cdip-classifier"}
### [RVL-CDIP-Classifier](rvl-cdip-classifier.qmd)
[Vision LLMs & prompt engineering]{.kicker}

A study of zero-shot document classification with vision LLMs. It covers 29 tracked prompt versions, accuracy checked on larger slices than the tuning set, cost per page, and Monte Carlo analysis of ensembles and routing.

[OpenRouter]{.tag} [Evaluation]{.tag} [Error analysis]{.tag}
:::
:::

## Data engineering & visualization {.group-title}

::: {.cards .cards-wide}
::: {.card cover="mailroom-corpus-eda"}
### [Mailroom-Corpus-EDA](mailroom-corpus-eda.qmd)
[Data engineering · dataset build, audit & publishing]{.kicker}

The data work behind the mailroom projects: 3,302 documents assembled from public sources, with stable identifiers, a record of how each label was made, and labels kept out of the text a model reads. An audit pipeline checks every number it publishes, and once caught itself reporting a false failure.

[Python]{.tag} [pandas]{.tag} [Hugging Face Hub]{.tag} [Provenance]{.tag}
:::

::: {.card cover="aeroglobe"}
### [AeroGlobe](aeroglobe.qmd)
[In active development · 3D flight data on a globe]{.kicker}

A browser globe for flight tracking, built around a static data pipeline so that flights can be replayed without an always-on server. An early version is live: it shows a short sample of real traffic recorded when the site was built and replays recorded tracks, and full-day playback is planned.

[TypeScript]{.tag} [CesiumJS]{.tag} [React]{.tag} [Data pipeline]{.tag}
:::

## Big data & distributed systems {.group-title}

::: {.cards .cards-wide}
::: {.card cover="mapreduce-reloaded"}
### [MapReduce-Reloaded](mapreduce-reloaded.qmd)
[In active development · distributed systems · Go & Python]{.kicker}

A from-scratch rebuild of Google's 2004 MapReduce, with a Go cluster and a Python reference. The paper mapping now includes 24 items, including performance experiments. S3 storage, compression, a VM evaluation and the final report are built; full Python worker parity remains a stretch goal.

[Go]{.tag} [Python]{.tag} [gRPC]{.tag} [Docker Compose]{.tag} [Fault tolerance]{.tag}
:::
:::

## Behavioral machine learning {.group-title}

::: {.cards .cards-wide}
::: {.card cover="psychometric-digital-twin"}
### [Psychometric Digital Twin](psychometric-digital-twin.qmd)
[Behavioral ML research · UW–Madison]{.kicker}

Can an LLM, told who a survey respondent is in the second person, predict that person's own communication-apprehension scores? Seven classical models against LLM personas on 241 respondents, with error checked by demographic group. The personas did not beat simple baselines.

[scikit-learn]{.tag} [XGBoost]{.tag} [SHAP]{.tag} [vLLM]{.tag}
:::
:::

## Cognitive neuroscience {.group-title}

::: {.cards .cards-wide}
::: {.card cover="natd"}
### [The Neural Architecture of Truth and Deception](natd.qmd)
[Cognitive neuroscience research · UW–Parkside]{.kicker}

Nine participants each talked to two chatbots told either to help or to deceive. Exam scores rose after the helpful personas and fell after the deceitful ones, and almost nobody flagged the deceit.

[Truth-Default Theory]{.tag} [Chatbot personas]{.tag} [Pilot study]{.tag}
:::
:::

## LLM agent design {.group-title}

::: {.cards .cards-wide}
::: {.card cover="llm-personas"}
### [MORNINGSTAR](llm-personas.qmd)
[Persona framework · prompt architecture]{.kicker}

A courtroom of LLM personas that argue, vote, and issue a written ruling on engineering decisions, plus a tamper-evident log library the runner does not call yet. One model plays every seat, and it has not yet been tested against a single-prompt baseline.

[Prompt design]{.tag} [Python]{.tag} [Hash chains]{.tag}
